markets.summary: US stocks rallied on Friday, with the Nasdaq up 2.3% and the S&P 500 up 1.6% as tech shares swung higher again after Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Even so, Nvidia ended November down nearly 28% and the S&P 500 remains in correction territory after the month's sell-off.

stories.headline: Chinese chip stocks post record one-day gains
stories.summary: Chinese chip stocks notched their biggest ever one-day gains after a rare midday statement from the State Council stressed market support and pledged liquidity. The intervention signals Beijing's willingness to step in as the AI-driven sell-off rattles Asian tech.

stories.headline: S&P cuts France's outlook to negative
stories.summary: S&P Global lowered its outlook on France's credit rating to negative, citing political instability. The agency says the turmoil will make it harder for Paris to bring down its public deficit.

sources.title: S&P cuts France outlook to negative

stories.headline: Dangote refinery heads for Africa's biggest IPO
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote plans to take his mega-refinery public in a listing that could value it at about $47 billion. It is expected to be the largest stock market listing in Africa's history.

us.headline: Asylum all but ended; advocates turn to the Supreme Court
us.summary: Trump's asylum ban, mass firings and new legal manoeuvres have effectively ended asylum in the US, and advocates are looking to the Supreme Court to restore it. The high court's response will decide whether the policy shift becomes permanent.

sources.title: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it

us.headline: Black Friday spending set for a record despite inflation
us.summary: Retailers expect record Black Friday spending as value-hunting shoppers turn out despite higher prices. Food, travel and gift costs are all up this year as inflation and the Iran-war energy shock squeeze household budgets.

us.headline: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec religious-symbols ban
us.summary: Canada's Supreme Court largely upheld Quebec's Bill 21, which bans public servants from wearing religious symbols. Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers had challenged the law as a breach of their fundamental rights.

sources.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants

uk.headline: Badenoch makes Tory candidates pledge to scrap net zero
uk.summary: Kemi Badenoch says Conservative candidates must sign a 'candidates covenant' that includes scrapping net-zero targets. She argues it will rebuild trust in the party, but some former MPs have criticised the move.

sources.title: Tory candidates must sign pledge to scrap net-zero targets, says Badenoch

uk.headline: Centrica warns of Rough job losses after storage snub
uk.summary: Centrica says hundreds of jobs at its Rough gas storage site off the Yorkshire coast are at risk after the government rejected a support deal. Centrica has criticised the decision.

sources.title: Centrica warns on jobs after government snubs Rough gas storage deal

uk.headline: Cyber incident takes DWP benefits and pensions services offline
uk.summary: Millions have lost access to online benefits and pension services after the Department for Work and Pensions took systems offline following what the work and pensions secretary called a 'serious cyber incident'. Services were still down on Saturday morning, and the outage is one of several hitting western institutions, including the US Treasury and Fifa.

europe.headline: Ukraine offers a Black Sea ceasefire
europe.summary: Kyiv has submitted an offer for a ceasefire in the Black Sea to allow food exports and shared the details with allies, and is awaiting Moscow's response. Air attacks are nonetheless intensifying, with Russia saying it downed 1,200 drones aimed at Moscow overnight.

sources.title: Ukraine submits Black Sea ceasefire offer, awaits Russian response

europe.headline: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy
europe.summary: Low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic has filed for bankruptcy after failing to secure funding as jet fuel costs soared. EasyJet's boss has warned that more airlines could follow.

europe.summary: Comments by Jared Kushner on Vladimir Putin drew anger across Europe, with a Kyiv lawmaker calling for him to be replaced as peace envoy. Zelensky separately told the BBC the US is not pushing Russia hard enough and called the Trump-Putin friendship 'strange'.

middle_east.headline: Kuwait summons Iran's envoy as US enforces blockade
middle_east.summary: Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over what it called continued Iranian attacks, while the US disabled a ship in the Gulf of Oman trying to leave Iran. Tehran has vowed to confront the blockade of its ports.

middle_east.summary: Riyadh is shifting Vision 2030 from 'spending and delivery at any cost' to 'at the right cost', according to the economy minister, under economic and security pressure. The recalibration comes as Houthi attacks test the kingdom's image of security.

middle_east.summary: An Israeli strike on a Doctors Without Borders clinic in Gaza killed two of its staff. MSF says the premises were clearly marked and their location known to the Israeli military.

energy.summary: Octopus Energy's chief executive has called for the regulatory asset value (RAV) model used to fund UK networks to be scrapped. RAV underpins how network companies earn returns on investment, so any change would shape the grid build-out.
